index_line: - [[dynaudio-special-forty]] — 6 Ω, LW ±2.2 dB, f3 52 Hz, 83 dB sens, pref 4.7 (EAC); 3 measurers, cabinet resonance near 500 Hz
source_index_lines: - [[eac-dynaudio-special-forty]] — Erin's Audio Corner Klippel review, 2023 (Tier A)
- [[tas-dynaudio-special-forty]] — The Absolute Sound review, Chris Martens, 2018 (Tier D)
brand_notes: Special Forty (2017 40th-anniversary, now Editions series, Current at dynaudio.com) is 6 ohm; Dynaudio's current range elsewhere often 4 ohm (Heritage Special 4 ohm, out of scope). Evoke 10/20 are 6 ohm, rear-ported, current ($1,699/$2,399) but lack Tier A/B (see no-tier-ab sidecars). Tier-A/B data show 1.6-2.8 dB lower sensitivity than the 86 dB claim (mfr-dynaudio-special-forty, eac-dynaudio-special-forty). Stereophile heard cabinet-wall resonance (stereophile-dynaudio-special-forty). Warranty 5 yr / 8 yr registered per soundstage-dynaudio-special-forty.
takeaways: LW +/-2.2 dB, f3 52 Hz, sensitivity 83.2 dB (EAC Klippel) vs 86 dB claim; NRC 83.6 and Stereophile 84.4 agree it is low.
Min impedance 4.9 Ω (EAC, Stereophile) with EPDR min 2.5 Ω: demanding for a 6 Ω rating; not flagged (>=4.8 Ω).
Cabinet sidewall mode near 512 Hz and 700 Hz port spike (Stereophile); audible congestion per JA only; SoundStage and TAS did not hear it.
Pref 4.7 / 6.7 with sub; early-reflection dip 3.4 dB flagged at 1.5 kHz.
Status/price uncertain: Dynaudio lists Current; $3,599 at Audio Vision SF vs $2,999 launch; TMR sold out.
conflicts: Cabinet resonance audible to Stereophile only
Status: limited edition (Stereophile) vs not limited (SoundStage) vs Current (Dynaudio)
